_doc: Legislation to Watch: steward-curated, neutral. `why` says what a bill changes for practitioners, drawn from the Legislative Counsel's Digest; never whether it should pass. Keep six or fewer; retire an item when its bill leaves the Governor's desk or stops moving.
heading: On the Governor's desk
dek: Six of the housing bills awaiting the Governor's signature or veto that change day-to-day practice most. Each opens to its full record.

items.title: Density bonus by determination, and by floor area
items.why: Would require a city or county to grant a density bonus, incentives and waivers once it determines an application meets the law's criteria, let an applicant who submits a base density study take the bonus as added floor area ratio, and apply the bonus across sites that are part of the same housing development.

items.title: CEQA exemption for affordable housing, extended to 2037
items.why: Would extend the existing CEQA exemption for qualifying affordable housing projects to January 1, 2037, and add public university and public college housing projects that meet its requirements.

items.title: Two plan checks, then a decision
items.why: Would limit building permit plan check reviews to two, bar inspections from requiring changes that depart from approved plans except as specified, and set post-entitlement permit timelines of 30 business days for projects of 25 units or fewer and 45 business days for larger ones.

items.title: Farmworker housing in the tax credit program
items.why: An urgency bill. Would require CTCAC to consider a farmworker housing type in its scoring, using the rural set-aside's amenity points, and for taxable years from 2027 would bar low-income housing tax credits for farmworker housing used to meet the H-2A employer housing requirement.

items.title: A property tax exemption for moderate-income rentals
items.why: An urgency bill. Would create a partial welfare exemption, equal to the value of units serving low- and moderate-income households, for lien dates from 2027 through 2029, lasting 15 years from the first filing and backed by owner certifications.

items.title: Missing Middle Townhome Ownership Act
items.why: Would create a ministerial approval path, including ministerial tentative and final maps, for townhome projects of up to three stories on parcels as small as 600 square feet that meet objective standards. San Francisco is exempt.
